speaker: dave
text: Hey Maya, you will not believe what I just did. I dialed into a BBS over radio.

speaker: maya
text: No way. Like an actual bulletin board? With a modem and everything?

speaker: dave
text: Yeah! It's called the AXIS BBS. It runs on a little ESP32 board with a color screen.

speaker: maya
text: Wait, a tiny board is running the whole thing? How does it even connect?

speaker: dave
text: Through the LoRa modem. I typed A T D T, and it started training, and then it said CONNECT.

speaker: maya
text: Okay, that is wild. What did the connect line say?

speaker: dave
text: CONNECT LORA S F 7. It picks a speed tier by itself, depending on the signal.

speaker: maya
text: Ha, so it slows down when the signal gets bad. Just like the old modems.

speaker: dave
text: Exactly. And then the ANSI art loads, all in color. It looks so good.

speaker: maya
text: Stop it. I miss that. What can you actually do on there?

speaker: dave
text: There are message bases, a file area, door games, even a voting booth for new users.

speaker: maya
text: Did you post anything? Or leave a message?

speaker: dave
text: Yeah, I left a hello in the general base. Felt like 1994 all over again.

speaker: maya
text: Honestly, calling a BBS over radio is the coolest thing I've heard all week.

speaker: dave
text: Right? No internet, no cell tower. Just two radios and a lot of static.

speaker: maya
text: Okay, I'm sold. Send me the number, and I'm calling tonight.
